messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: R Shiny server connect with Database
parts:
Depends on your choice of database, but you should be able to connect to the database with shiny in the exact same way you would when doing analyses in R.

You'll have to manage the database separately.

As far as anonymizing data, that is somewhat vague.

You'd want to make sure that:

1.  Your database and R's connection to it is secure.  
2.  You use HTTPS to send and receive data.  This will require you deploying shiny server behind a SSL certificate.  Or using shinyapps.io, which uses TLS by default.
3.  If needed, you may want your DB to be encrypted at rest.


The last step is more complicated as it requires knowledge beyond R/Shiny to make sure everything works.


Erik

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: R Shiny server connect with Database
parts:
Depends on your needs.

If you have a small budget and are new to databases and privacy is important I'd recommend something like:

AWS RDS w/ encryption at rest turned on.
In same VPC, host a small EC2 isntance w/ your shiny app.
If SSL is new to you, you can put your app behind an AWS load balancer and install an SSL certificate on it.


If data security is very important and this is new to you I'd recommend hiring someone.  None of this is super complicated but there is a bit of a learning curve, so w/ data that needs to be private it may be a lot to learn all at once.
Erik
